one_line: Fourth Sikh Guru who developed Ramdaspur (later Amritsar) around its sacred sarovar.

appearance.age_look: Appears in his mid-40s to early-50s, medium height, lean but sturdy from active work and travel.
appearance.face: Oval face with a calm, luminous expression; warm wheatish-brown complexion; large gentle anime-style eyes with a soft but focused gaze; straight nose; neatly kept medium-length beard that is combed and slightly rounded at the end; subtle smile conveying humility and compassion.
appearance.hair: Long dark-brown hair tied up neatly in a topknot completely wrapped under a simple, medium-sized white turban (dastaar) with smooth folds, no ornamentation; a thin white patka-like undercloth peeks at the temples, giving a clean, composed look.
appearance.costume: He wears a long, knee-length Punjabi-style jama/kurta in soft off-white cotton with straight sleeves and a modest round neckline tied with a small cord, over a pair of loose, straight-cut churidar-style trousers in light beige; over this is a plain, unpatterned, mid-weight ochre-golden chadar (shawl) draped over both shoulders and wrapped once around his torso, with one end hanging forward over his left arm; simple dark-brown leather sandals on his feet; overall look is modest, practical, and suited to a 16th-century Punjab town environment, with no jewelry except a very thin, almost unobtrusive iron-like bangle on his right wrist.
appearance.signature: A rolled bundle of simple paper or bir-like manuscript tied with a cord, held together with a slender reed pen tucked under the cord, symbolizing his hymns and guidance in building Ramdaspur; he often carries it gently in his left hand or under his arm.

ref_desc: Guru Ram Das is a gentle, wheatish-complexioned man in his late-40s with a neatly rounded dark-brown beard, long hair wrapped in a plain white turban, wearing an off-white kurta, beige trousers, an ochre-golden shawl, dark-brown sandals, and carrying a rolled manuscript bundle with a reed pen.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Guru Ram Das: a dignified, humble man in his late-40s with an oval face, warm wheatish-brown skin, large gentle eyes, and a neatly combed medium-length dark-brown beard rounded at the end, his long hair fully wrapped in a simple white turban with smooth folds and a thin undercloth showing at the temples; he wears a modest off-white knee-length Punjabi-style kurta with straight sleeves and a small tied neckline, loose light-beige churidar-style trousers, and an unpatterned ochre-golden cotton shawl draped over both shoulders and wrapped once around his torso, one end hanging over his left arm, plus simple dark-brown leather sandals and a very thin iron-like bangle on his right wrist; in his left hand or tucked under his arm is his signature rolled manuscript bundle tied with a cord, with a slender reed pen visible under the cord, and the colour palette emphasizes off-white, light beige, ochre-golden, dark brown and soft white, shown from front, side and back to clearly display face, hair, clothing and the manuscript prop.
